entities.name: CpROM1
observations: Cryptosporidium parvum rhomboid1 interacted with CpGP900 in yeast two-hybrid assays and promoted appearance of a CpGP900 cleavage product during mammalian-cell co-expression; evidence is heterologous-cell based.
CpROM1 was localized to micronemes in sporozoites and intracellular merozoites, providing spatial compatibility with micronemal CpGP900.
No purified-enzyme assay, catalytic-mutant control, endogenous perturbation, or mapped cleavage site was identified in the retrieved evidence.

entities.name: CpGP900
observations: CpGP900 is a microneme protein that produced a cleavage product when co-expressed with CpROM1, but not when expressed alone, in the 2016 heterologous-cell study.
Endogenous GP900 is cleaved in the secretory pathway before extracellular release; the responsible protease was not identified.

entities.name: PMID:27502595
observations: The 2016 study reported CpROM1-CpGP900 interaction and a CpGP900 cleavage product upon co-expression, leading the authors to identify CpGP900 as a CpROM1 substrate.

entities.name: PMID:34966810
observations: The 2021 study localized CpROM1 to micronemes of sporozoites and intracellular merozoites by immunofluorescence and immunogold electron microscopy.

entities.name: PMID:35581607
observations: The 2022 study showed endogenous GP900 cleavage in the secretory pathway before extracellular release, without identifying CpROM1 as the responsible enzyme.
